name: Sven Titz; Kalina Oroschakoff; Jean-Christophe Bott
frames_manual: An argument of caution in the attribution of the event in Blatten to climate change. The role of climate change in the Blatten event is complex. One the one side climate change is leading to glacier melt, precipitation falling as rain instead of snow which destabilise the mountains. However, the Blatten event is statistically rare and hence the role of climate change is complex. Researchers agree that climate change has a role in rockslide but  the relationship between climate change and rockfalls, rockslides and debris flows is complex. There are many indications that these hazards are increasing in general, but not everywhere and not all of them. It is unclear how severely the steep face of the Kleines Nesthorn was affected by the thawing of the permafrost. There are also other phenomena at play in the mountains such as the weathering that can also lead to movement and landslides.
frames: Climate change increases hazards in the Alps; however, establishing a direct causal link to a single event like Blatten remains difficult.
